title: Talk instead of typing, without your voice leaving this computer
blurb: Claude Code can already listen — just type /voice, and that is the better choice for most people. Set this up only if you need your voice to stay on your own machine, or if /voice doesn't work for you.
newcomerProblem: You want to talk instead of type, but your voice can't be sent to a server — or /voice isn't available to you.

insteadOf.summary: Claude Code has voice built in. Type /voice, then hold space and speak. It needs no setup, understands coding words, and is free.
useThisWhen: Your voice has to stay on this computer. The built-in one sends your recording to Anthropic to be turned into text; this one never sends anything anywhere.
You sign in with an API key, Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry rather than a Claude.ai account — the built-in one is unavailable then.
You're working over SSH or on a remote machine, where the built-in one can't reach your microphone.
Your workplace has turned the built-in one off.
You also want to talk in your browser, your editor, and everywhere else — not only in Claude Code.

tryThisExplain: Try the built-in one first — it needs no setup. If it isn't available or you need your voice to stay on this computer, run .claude/scripts/talk.sh instead.
explain: Claude Code already has listening built in, and for most people that is the one to use. This kit is the alternative for when it can't be used: your computer listens through the microphone and types out what you say, wherever your cursor happens to be. The listening happens entirely on your own machine, so no recording is ever sent anywhere, and it works in every other program too.
honestLimit: The built-in /voice is easier and understands coding words better. This one needs a one-time setup, is less accurate, and types into whatever window you're in — neither adds a microphone button inside Claude Code.
uninstallNote: This removes the shortcut. Anything you installed on your computer yourself stays where it is.
